title: Color as a Key Factor in Creating Sustainable Living Spaces for Seniors

findings.antecedent: living room interior concept with monochromatic, monotonous grey composition (Interior 1)
findings.mechanism: perceived as sad, depressing, unstimulating, and uninspiring due to lack of colors, accents, and contrasts
findings.quote: None of the surveyed seniors decided to choose this interior concept.

findings.antecedent: living room interior concepts dominated by distinctly warm or distinctly cold tones
findings.mechanism: implied lack of harmony or balance
findings.quote: Interiors dominated by distinctly warm or distinctly cold tones were also not popular.

findings.antecedent: living room interior concepts with strong tonal contrasts or clear contrasts of saturation and brightness
findings.quote: seniors did not choose interiors with strong tonal contrasts or clear contrasts of saturation and brightness.

findings.antecedent: harmoniously composed living room interior concepts based on colors of similar tones, emphasizing warm and cold shade contrasts
findings.mechanism: aligns with Le Corbusier's color theory, providing aesthetic balance and visual comfort
findings.quote: They preferred harmoniously composed spaces, based on colors of similar tones, which emphasize each other through contrasts of warm and cold shades

findings.antecedent: living room interior concepts with colors from nature, earth tones, and natural materials (wood, wool, fabrics, leather, greenery)
findings.mechanism: seniors prefer a color environment associated with nature
findings.quote: The greatest interest was aroused by compositions with colors coming from nature, the colors of the earth, and the colors of natural materials

findings.antecedent: colors from the range of shades corresponding to short wavelengths (blues and greens) as favorite colors
findings.mechanism: hues predominate in natural landscape, considered neutral, complement each other, do not tire eyes, and have a calming impact
findings.quote: A total of 57 out of 90 seniors chose colors from the range of shades corresponding to short wavelengths—blues and greens.

findings.antecedent: shades of blue as favorite colors
findings.mechanism: most liked, calming impact, natural association
findings.quote: Shades of blue were chosen by 26 seniors as their favorite colors.

findings.antecedent: the color purple (among cool colors) as a favorite color
findings.mechanism: implied aesthetic dislike or difficulty in perception
findings.quote: Among the cool colors that turned out to be the least liked by seniors was the color purple—only one person chose it.

findings.antecedent: colors from the range of shades corresponding to medium and/or long wavelengths (red, orange, yellow) as favorite colors
findings.mechanism: less preferred than shades of blue and green, despite being easier to distinguish for seniors
findings.quote: these colors turned out to be less preferred by them than shades of blue and green.

findings.mechanism: implied aesthetic dislike or potential for irritation with long-term exposure

findings.antecedent: pure, saturated red as a favorite color
findings.mechanism: implied aesthetic dislike or potential for overstimulation
findings.quote: only six people chose pure, saturated red.

findings.antecedent: warm earth hues (warm browns, ochres, siennas, rusty reds, oranges) as favorite colors
findings.mechanism: confirms inclination towards colors associated with nature
findings.quote: In the group of favorited warm colors, many earth hues appeared—warm browns, ochres, siennas, rusty reds, and oranges.
Interestingly, seven people, including three men, chose pink.

findings.antecedent: grey as a favorite achromatic color
findings.quote: grey was selected by eight people

findings.antecedent: black as a favorite achromatic color
findings.mechanism: implied aesthetic dislike or association with darkness/confinement

findings.antecedent: white as a favorite achromatic color
findings.mechanism: implied aesthetic dislike or association with monotony/lack of stimulation
a living space devoid of colors is far from the natural human environment, lacking wealth, diversity, and shades
findings.quote: The results of the study are evidence of the lack of acceptance by seniors of achromatic or monochromatic surroundings.

findings.antecedent: living room interior design (Concept 20) with varied shades of white, natural wool, creamy, ecru, light beiges, browns, matte/shimmering greys, copper, black, and natural greens, with interior-exterior interpenetration
findings.mechanism: associated with nature, offering diversity and visual comfort
findings.quote: This composition was liked the most and was chosen by 11 seniors.

stimuli.description: 20 visualizations of living room interior designs, differing in style and color, presented as printouts on separate sheets of paper

tables.description: Summary of survey results showing total preferences, women's preferences, and men's preferences for 20 different interior color concepts.

limitations: The survey was conducted among culturally homogenous participants; therefore, cultural differences in color perception and preferences were not considered in this study.
